headline: Service strength continues as margins compress
summary_short: Otis reported Q2 FY2026 net sales of $3,859M, up 7.3% y/y and 8.2% q/q, with GAAP diluted EPS of $1.12 (+13.1% y/y) even as adjusted EPS fell 4% to $1.01 on higher interest and tax.
summary_long: Net sales rose 7.3% y/y to $3,859M as Service grew 11% (9% organic) across all lines, while New Equipment was flat (-1% organic), improving sequentially. GAAP operating profit rose $28M as prior-year UpLift and separation costs rolled off; adjusted operating profit fell $25M as Service investment and corporate items outweighed New Equipment softness, cutting adjusted margin 180bp to 15.2%. GAAP EPS of $1.12 reflects the same comp; adjusted EPS fell 4% to $1.01 on higher interest and tax, partly offset by FX and a lower share count. Cash of $813M fell 2.5% q/q after $407M of buybacks. Otis revised FY2026 outlook to net sales of $15.1-15.3B, adjusted EPS of $4.01-4.05, and adjusted free cash flow of $1.50-1.55B.

drivers.explanation: Growth driven by Service across all lines, with double-digit modernization and repair growth and accelerating maintenance; New Equipment improved sequentially but a high-teens China decline weighed on it.
GAAP EPS gain reflects the absence of prior-year UpLift transformation costs and separation-related adjustments; adjusted EPS instead fell on higher interest expense and a higher tax rate.
GAAP operating profit rose on the same absent prior-year one-time items; adjusted operating profit fell as Service investment and corporate items outweighed New Equipment softness.

Company revised FY2026 outlook (net sales $15.1-15.3B, adjusted EPS $4.01-4.05) citing continued investment in Service quality, pricing and digital initiatives, and a "measured approach" to second-half visibility.
